decisions.reason: SOL keeps the image and sense; a singular ger reads naturally for the Korean subject.
SOL keeps the early-before-sunrise timing in natural phrasing.
SOL keeps the night-breaking hoofbeats without changing the action.
“Some hundred” softens 백여 기, which indicates more than a hundred; BASE preserves the quantity.
SOL keeps the pale-faced emperor receiving reports while tightening the sentence.
“Mobilizing” fits the immediate military action commanded in the source.
SOL drops the source’s image of the sounds vanishing as if washed away.
SOL omits the careful steps of those backing away.
SOL drops 비스듬히: the Emperor is leaning at an angle against the throne.
SOL keeps the Emperor’s expectation and surprise at how quickly they moved.
SOL keeps the faction’s size and methodical nature.
The source introduces an unspecified religious movement; BASE’s “a” preserves that, while SOL’s “the” implies an already identified one.
SOL combines the two sentences without changing the Demonic Cult’s departure for the Central Plains.
“Cultists” preserves the group’s identity more directly than “so-called heretics.”
SOL softens the contempt in 촌무지렁이 and replaces the specific spears and swords with generic blades.
SOL adds “seemed” as an unsupported hedge and drops the request to order a campaign.
SOL keeps that Baek Yeon opposed joining the war more strongly than anyone.
SOL keeps the unusual earnestness of Baek Yeon’s plea without changing the outcome.
SOL keeps both reasons and preserves the conversational delivery.
“Someone to watch” is a natural recast of 요주의 인물.
SOL adds “he believed” and removes the source’s “by extension” link between the Great Nation and the people.
“It’s the truth” loses the sense of 어쩔 수 없는: this was an unavoidable fact.
SOL changes the pebble to a stone and loses the repeated smashing and battering.
SOL loses the source’s pointed, jagged quality and the pebble image established in the preceding line.
SOL adds “might,” weakening the source’s counterfactual that they would not have reached the present.
“Dwarf the Great Faction War” keeps the source’s comparison of the coming bloodshed.
“Fortunately” naturally preserves the source’s misfortune-within-misfortune relief.
The source says the troops are waiting for their command; SOL makes this indefinite as “orders.”
SOL keeps the Emperor rising despite his ailing condition in natural English.
SOL retains the white robe, golden dragon, and heavy armor while avoiding an awkward clothing transition.
SOL keeps the order to announce that the Emperor will lead the campaign personally.
SOL drops the effort and failed continuation conveyed by Baek Yeon struggling to force out the words.
SOL keeps the Emperor’s head shake and Baek Yeon’s constrained reaction.
SOL keeps the sense that little time remains for the Emperor’s future.
SOL keeps the temporary return of the Emperor’s will to live.
SOL drops that the promise was made to the Emperor, an explicit relationship in the source.
SOL omits the report reaching the narrator’s ear and that his eyes had been closed.
SOL keeps Hyuk Mujin’s grave expression and the urgency it conveys.
SOL follows the project’s established “Imperial Capital” rendering.
“Their sources” narrows 정보력; BASE preserves the broader intelligence-gathering capability.
SOL keeps the conversation’s purpose of putting the narrator at ease.
“Heh” better preserves the wry, laugh-like reaction than SOL’s surprised “Huh.”
SOL keeps the narrator swallowing a laugh without adding the unsupported quality “dry.”
SOL preserves the incongruous breezy voice and the Emperor waiting and laughing.
